about: Is your phone listening for ads? Factory #33, backlog row 37, slug phonelistening. One hard idea: studies found no sign apps send your audio out, and the most famous 'we listen' ad pitch (Cox Media Group's Active Listening) turned out, per the FTC, to use no voice data at all; it resold email lists from data brokers, which is what ads actually run on. Hero: the cut-paper 'Active Listening' box wired to the phone, torn open by the FTC to spill email lists. Sources (read 2026-11-16) in BRIEF.md section 3. Planned silences: 0.5 s after the hook (frame-0 hit), 0.6 s after 'what you say.' (dip: the box lights up), 0.5 s after 'no voice data.' (tear), 1.2 s after 'data brokers.' (hero: lists spill, summary drawing, screenshot hold), 0.45 s after 'camera's on.' (dot pulse). Narration-led: record the voice first and key every visual beat to its word times; re-chain `at` to the real Ming takes.
